chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdul Rahman ibn Al-Hajjaj who said, 'I heard Abbad Al-Basri saying,'

Ja'far (peace be upon him) was saying: 'The Hadd penalty is deferred from him by the measure of his share in her, and he is struck with what is other than that, meaning regarding the man when he has intercourse with a slave girl in which he has a share.'
ai.seo_question: What is the Hadd penalty for a man having intercourse with his partially owned slave girl?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the principle of proportional liability in Islamic jurisprudence, where the fixed Hadd penalty for fornication is deferred for the portion of the slave girl owned by others, leaving only the Ta'zir (discretionary) punishment for the owner's share. It highlights the nuanced application of penal codes in the context of partial ownership, reflecting the practical legal reasoning of Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) regarding property rights and bodily autonomy. This ruling underscores the distinction between the rights of God (Haqq Allah) and the rights of individuals (Haqq al-Adami) in determining the severity of punishment.
